'''Beulah Russell''', christened '''Beatrice Beulah Russell''' and also known as '''Bulah Russell''', (October 22, 1878 – February 22, 1940) was an American [[mathematician]].<ref name="Andrews">{{Cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Russell_Beulah/|title=Beulah Russell (1878 - 1940) - Biography - MacTutor History of Mathematics|date=December 2021|last1=Robertson|first1=Edmund|last2=O’Connor|first2=John| author-link=Edmund F. Robertson|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220502183249/https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Russell_Beulah/ |archive-date=2022-05-02 }}</ref>

==Education==
Beulah graduated from [[Randolph College|Randolph–Macon Woman's College]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in 1903, and graduated from the [[University of Chicago]] with a [[Master of Arts]] in 1919.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://virginiachronicle.com/?a=d&d=RNL19250724.1.19&e=-------en-20--1--txt-txIN--------|title=Richmond News Leader 24 July 1925 — Virginia Chronicle: Digital Newspaper Archive|website=virginiachronicle.com}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IDPPAAAAMAAJ&dq=Bulah+Russell+mathematics&pg=PA17|title=BULLETIN; The College of William and Mary in Virginia, Volume XX, Number 1|pages=17|date=April 1926|website=Google Books}}</ref>

==Career==
From 1903 to 1905 Beulah taught at [[Lafayette College]] as an instructor in mathematics. From 1905 to 1909 she taught at [[Grenada College]] as a professor of mathematics. From 1909 to 1925 she taught at [[Randolph College|Randolph–Macon Woman's College]] as an instructor of mathematics and an adjunct professor of mathematics. In 1925 she became an associate professor of mathematics at the [[College of William & Mary]].<ref name="auto"/><ref name="Andrews"/>

In a 1923 edition of ''[[The American Mathematical Monthly]]'' it is recorded that Beulah was elected to membership in the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mQxLAAAAYAAJ&dq=%22beulah+russell%22+1923+journal&pg=PA349|title=The American Mathematical Monthly: The Official Journal of the Mathematical Association of America, Volume 30|pages=347–349|date=1923|website=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>

In 1930 Beulah became the first female professor to attend the [[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]] Colloquium held in St Andrews, Scotland.<ref name="Andrews"/>
